profile.campus: AWS Northern Virginia (Data Center Alley) -- US-EAST-1 region, Loudoun / Prince William / Fairfax counties
profile.address: 13850, Redskin Drive, Herndon, Fairfax County, Virginia, 20171
profile.reading:
This building is one of the data center structures Amazon Web Services operates in Northern Virginia, within the corridor of eastern Loudoun, Prince William, and Fairfax counties that the data center industry calls Data Center Alley, described in trade press as the largest concentration of data centers in the world. AWS traces its Virginia data center presence back to 2006, making this one of the company's original hyperscale cloud regions, now designated US-EAST-1. The corridor grew up around the MAE-East internet exchange point that formed near Tysons and Ashburn in the 1990s, which drew network carriers and later cloud and colocation operators to locate near dense fiber connectivity.

AWS's own public affairs materials, published on aboutamazon.com, state that the company invested $51.9 billion in capital and operating expenses on its Virginia data center infrastructure between 2011 and 2021, and in January 2023 announced a further $35 billion committed to build additional data center campuses across Virginia through 2040. AWS reports its Virginia operations generated $8.2 billion in regional GDP over 2011 to 2021, supported an average of 7,340 full time equivalent jobs at local businesses across that period, and employed 8,710 people directly in the state by 2021, a figure AWS later put at more than 8,800. In 2022, AWS paid $334 million in Virginia business personal property tax. AWS also states it operates 18 solar farms in Virginia generating roughly 2.9 million megawatt hours of clean energy annually, enough by its own estimate to power about 276,000 homes, and that approximately 70 percent of global internet traffic moves through data centers located in the state.

AWS has not published a street address, opening date, floor area, or IT power rating for this individual building, and no county or state economic development record found for this page breaks the Virginia AWS footprint down building by building. What is documented is that this structure sits within the AWS data center footprint the company has confirmed for the Loudoun, Prince William, and Fairfax county corridor, described by the investment, employment, and tax figures above, which report the regional AWS buildout rather than this specific structure.

profile.regional_context: Northern Virginia is described in trade press as the largest data center market in the world by capacity, anchored by the Loudoun County corridor known as Data Center Alley and now extending into Prince William, Fairfax, and neighboring counties. Alongside AWS, the corridor hosts large campuses operated by Digital Realty, Equinix, Microsoft, Google, Meta, QTS, and CloudHQ, among others. Power for the region comes primarily from Dominion Energy, which has repeatedly identified data center demand as the fastest growing category on its system and has sought new transmission and generation capacity to keep pace. Virginia exempts qualifying data center equipment purchases from state and local sales and use tax under a program administered by the Virginia Economic Development Partnership, an incentive credited by local officials with accelerating the buildout. Local zoning disputes over new campuses, water use for cooling, and Dominion grid capacity have been a recurring subject in Loudoun and Prince William county government since the early 2020s, reported by Virginia Business, Data Center Frontier, and Inside Climate News.

reading.body:
AWS operates this facility within Northern Virginia's Data Center Alley, a region spanning Loudoun, Prince William, and Fairfax counties that trade press identifies as the world's largest concentration of data center capacity. The building sits in a corridor that formed around the MAE-East internet exchange near Tysons and Ashburn in the 1990s and has hosted AWS's US-EAST-1 region, one of the company's original hyperscale cloud regions, since 2006. AWS does not publish IT power capacity, floor area, opening date, or facility role at the individual building level, and no county or state record breaks its Virginia operations down building by building.

AWS's documented Virginia footprint reflects $51.9 billion in capital and operating expenses from 2011 to 2021, with a further $35 billion committed through 2040. The company reported 8,710 direct employees in Virginia by 2021 and paid $334 million in state business personal property tax in 2022. AWS operates 18 solar farms in Virginia that the company states generate roughly 2.9 million megawatt hours of clean energy annually. Power for the region comes from Dominion Energy, which has identified data center demand as its fastest growing load category and has sought new transmission and generation capacity to meet it.

This specific facility's individual capacity, opening timeline, and tenancy are not published. Virginia ranked 24th among US states by published data center capacity as of this writing, with 23 of 326 mapped facilities reporting power figures totaling 1,375 megawatts. This building cannot be sized or ranked independently of the broader AWS Virginia campus cluster it belongs to, whose growth has driven recurring local disputes over zoning, water use for cooling, and regional grid constraints since the early 2020s.
